title: Japanese Black Pine: Ancient Black Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: Trained into shapes weather never would: a snow-roped pine in Kanazawa, a tide-garden giant in Tokyo, Nara's fattest survivor. Five mapped, four cities.
intro: Pinus thunbergii is the pine of the Japanese coast, tough enough for salt spray and heavy snow, and gardeners have spent centuries training it into shapes weather alone never would. Kanazawa strings ropes from a pole above its Karasaki pine every November so wet snow cannot break the limbs, the yukitsuri rigging that has become the picture of the city in winter; nearby, a Maeda lord is said to have raised another pine on a mound of earth and stripped the soil away, leaving forty-odd roots standing clear of the ground. Tokyo's grows in a garden the bay still floods daily on purpose, planted around 1709 and spent three centuries spreading rather than climbing. Nara's is simply the fattest survivor of a planting habit with no purpose but looking right: three and a half metres round, roughly two hundred and fifty years old. Five mapped so far, across four cities.
